data.Documented value: Competitive features of country associations based on the Global Competitiveness Index: the case of the United States – Mexico – Canada Agreement

Modern architecture of the world economy is determined not only by the indicators of development of individual national economies and not only by their individual efforts, but also by coordinated efforts of several countries, such as trade agreements. One of such agreements that should lead to freer market relations, fairer trade and sustainable economic growth in the region, better resolution of international disputes, environmental protection, intellectual property protection, etc., is the United States – Mexico – Canada Agreement (USMCA). The aim of this paper is an attempt to analyze the level of global competitiveness of intergovernmental associations (agreements) as influential participants in the international market. To do this, the concepts of “competitive power of the country” and “competitive power of international integration groups” are compared with the concept of firm competitiveness. The competitiveness of the country association was analyzed through the example of the USMCA based on The Global Competitiveness Report 2019 and The Global Competitiveness Index 4.0. used in it. The paper also examines the global challenges and obstacles affecting the level of competitiveness and competitive advantage that each country receives when participating in an international integration agreement. This analysis helps explain real competitive processes in the global economy.

data.Documented value: The Business of Schooling: Marketing in Canadian Independent Schools

This study explores the response of school administrators to the rapid infusion of marketing and business ideals and practices into the Canadian independent school system. As a mixed-methods study, a survey of CAIS schools (Canadian Association of Independent Schools) provides an environmental scan of marketing approaches across the country, while three in-depth case studies provide specific detail about how administrator responses play out at specific school sites. Five approaches to school marketing emerge from the survey, ranging from strongly welfarist to strongly new managerial. An exclusively business-oriented approach exists opposite to welfarism on the continuum, but was not observed in this study. School placement along the continuum is largely determined by the school's local competitive market. Schools in markets characterized by low levels of competition tend to encourage a welfarist approach to school leadership while highly competitive markets tend to support a new managerial approach. Case study schools were selected to represent different marketing approaches, and findings support the correlation between market competition and continuum positioning. The professional biographies of school administrators, in particular Heads of schools, were also found to correlate with the observed marketing approach. The existence of a continuum of approaches to independent school marketing, and in particular the placement of competitively-based schools along this continuum, likely has implications for stakeholders. This study raises questions about the consequences for students, parents, teachers and administrators resulting from the shift from welfarism to new managerialism observed in highly competitive markets.

paragraphs: The Canadian Gaming Association, a prominent organization representing the gaming industry, is set to demonstrate its competitive features in the realm of international associations. This initiative aims to highlight the strengths and strategies employed by the association in fostering a competitive environment within the global market. The demonstration will serve as a platform for showcasing the association's commitment to maintaining a high level of competitiveness, ensuring fair trade practices, and promoting sustainable economic growth. [[S2|Problems and Perspectives in Management]]

The demonstration will be based on the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), a trade agreement that seeks to enhance market relations, fair trade, and sustainable economic growth in the region. The USMCA is a significant milestone in the modern architecture of the world economy, driven by coordinated efforts of several countries, including Canada, Mexico, and the United States. This agreement is designed to address various global challenges, such as international disputes, environmental protection, and intellectual property rights, among others. [[S2|Problems and Perspectives in Management]]

The demonstration will be conducted through the use of the Global Competitiveness Report 2019 and The Global Competitiveness Index 4.0, which are widely recognized as benchmarks for assessing the competitiveness of countries and international integration groups. These reports provide a comprehensive analysis of the level of competitiveness and competitive advantage that each country receives when participating in an international integration agreement. By examining the USMCA, the demonstration will help explain real competitive processes in the global economy. [[S2|Problems and Perspectives in Management]]

The demonstration will also explore the global challenges and obstacles that affect the level of competitiveness and competitive advantage that each country receives when participating in an international integration agreement. This analysis is crucial for understanding the real competitive processes in the global economy. The demonstration will provide insights into how these challenges and obstacles are addressed and overcome, thereby contributing to the development of more effective and sustainable international integration agreements. [[S2|Problems and Perspectives in Management]]

sections.heading: Christian Labour Association of Canada; Competing From the Outside
paragraphs: Canadian Gaming Association to Demonstrate Competitiveness From the Outside The Christian Labour Association of Canada (CLAC) is a relatively small but growing independent Canadian labor union that has attracted a great deal of criticism from many mainstream unions. CLAC's approach to labor relations is based on Christian principles, which emphasize cooperation and reconciliation over conflict and reject the socialist notion of class struggle. This approach has led the organization to develop a unique approach to labor relations that puts it at odds with traditional Canadian unions and labor organizations. This paper attempts to provide some insights on CLAC's competitiveness by squaring its alternative approach to labor relations with its strong growth relative to other unions. [[S3|MacSphere McMaster University]]

[[S3|MacSphere McMaster University]] The findings of this paper build on existing research and literature on CLAC's background and philosophical underpinnings and are based heavily on firsthand interviews with workers and union executives. The key findings of this paper are that CLAC's competitiveness is strongly related to its conciliatory brand of labor relations, its organizational structure, rooted in its founding role as a religiously based cultural institution, and its position on the outside of the Canadian Labour Congress (CLC) umbrella. Another important conclusion is that the competitiveness of unions is heavily influenced by its ability to align its values and organizational culture with the values and identities of workers and the specific regulatory and economic environment in which they work. [[S3|MacSphere McMaster University]] Canadian Gaming Association to Demonstrate Competitiveness From the Outside [[S3|MacSphere McMaster University]] The Canadian Gaming Association (CGA) is set to showcase its newfound competitiveness on the gaming scene, aiming to challenge the dominance of traditional gaming giants.

This initiative comes as the industry faces increasing competition from emerging platforms and innovative gaming experiences. The CGA's approach is characterized by a focus on innovation, accessibility, and community engagement, positioning itself as a leader in the rapidly evolving gaming landscape. [[S3|MacSphere McMaster University]] The association's strategy includes a series of events and exhibitions designed to attract new players and showcase the latest technologies. These events will feature cutting-edge gaming hardware, immersive virtual reality experiences, and interactive gaming installations that encourage player interaction and community building.

The CGA's commitment to inclusivity and accessibility is also evident in its efforts to provide affordable gaming options and support for players with disabilities. [[S3|MacSphere McMaster University]] The association's leadership team emphasizes the importance of fostering a positive gaming environment and promoting healthy gaming habits among its members. This approach is aimed at attracting a broader audience and building a more engaged community around the gaming industry. The CGA's initiatives are expected to not only boost its own competitiveness but also contribute to the overall growth of the gaming industry.
